title: FullCD on a compactification gives the ambient exceptional adjoint
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an integer $n\geq1$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$, using the valuation ring and chosen uniformizer of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] on which $\ell$ is invertible, let $X,Y$ be finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $S$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] finite-type $S$-morphism. Suppose a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ is given, with $j$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $p$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and suppose $\operatorname{FullCD}(p,A;c)$ [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] for some integer $c\geq0$. On the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the chosen compact-support candidate $Rf_{!,n}:=Rp_*j_!$, with derived direct image as in [def-weil-derived-direct-image] and extension by zero as in [def-weil-extension-by-zero], preserves set-indexed coproducts and has a right adjoint $Rf_n^\times$. These adjunctions form an ambient exceptional right adjoint datum [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] with distinguished compactification $(j,p)$ and bound $c$: the adjunctions for compactifications are canonically identified along their compact-support comparison isomorphisms, with compatible units and counits and the cocycle condition for refinements.

source.place: sk-prop-sf-existence, clause (b), the conditional ambient pro-etale adjoint. proof.text: Transport the first FullCD conjunct through the canonical intrinsic module equivalences and the single-object comparison, then use the classical/total derived homology comparison to obtain R^q p_*=0 for q>c on fixed-scalar sheaves. Properness supplies qcqs. The proved Grothendieck-valued pro-etale direct-image theorem gives preservation of coproducts and acyclicity of sums of injectives. Apply the proved finite-CD injective-coproduct criterion to obtain coproduct preservation of the unbounded total derived functor. Only the original-source conjunct of FullCD is needed.

Apply Grothendieck-derived Brown representability to the fixed-scalar total direct image in the site/Hom universe u+1. Transport the resulting left-adjoint instance through the intrinsic derived equivalence. Compose it with the existing unbounded open adjunction. Thus the distinguished compact-support candidate is a left adjoint and preserves coproducts of every indexing universe for which the colimit exists, as required by the unchanged statement.

For a proper map identifying two quasi-compact opens, form its pullback over the target open and the source-open section. The section is clopen. Take the adjoint mate of ordinary weakly-etale direct-image base change to obtain open-extension/pullback exchange, transport it through the coefficient equivalences, and descend the exact functors termwise. Taking its derived adjoint mate yields direct-image/open-restriction exchange. Apply exchange again to the Cartesian square with top identity and the clopen section. The clopen-component theorem preserves K-injective complexes under insertion and identifies ordinary pushforward after insertion with identity; exact-precomposition/derived-functor comparison therefore gives the unbounded clopen-section isomorphism. Compose these to identify open restriction of proper pushforward of extension by zero with the original complex.

The existing proper/open support theorem says the actual open-adjunction counit is invertible on those proper direct images. Combining it with the restriction isomorphism constructs an isomorphism between target extension by zero and proper direct image of source extension by zero. Obtain derived pushforward composition by uniqueness of right adjoints to the intrinsic pullback composition comparison. The open in each compactification is quasi-compact because f is quasi-compact. This gives an isomorphism of compact-support candidates for each refinement; a common refinement supplies an isomorphism between any two candidates.

For each compactification e choose a proved isomorphism t_e from its candidate to the distinguished candidate. Transport the distinguished adjunction along t_e, use its same right adjoint at every compactification, define theta(v:e→h)=t_e followed by inverse(t_h), and set rho(v) to the identity. The explicit formulas in Adjunction.ofNatIsoLeft and cancellation prove unit and counit compatibility, identity comparisons, and both cocycle equations. Together with the supplied FullCD witness these are every field of the unchanged ambient datum. Its definition prescribes coherent comparison isomorphisms, not equality with individual geometric refinement maps, so no coherence theorem for those individual maps is necessary.

tool_uses.why: Step 1: all constant-ring module categories are Grothendieck; a generic ringed-site tool, with no replacement in the existence unit.
Step 1: additivity and left exactness of the ordinary module direct image; a functor-construction tool.

Step 2: bounded-below filtered continuity for a qcqs morphism, specialized to the constant condensed finite ring and degree-zero finite partial sums; this supplies continuity, not an exceptional adjoint or comparison theorem.
Step 2: geometric coefficient pullback identifies the constant condensed finite ring with the constant ring sheaf, coherently under scheme maps.
Step 3: termwise sums represent coproducts in the unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck category; generic homological algebra.
Step 3: finite cohomological dimension makes an arbitrary complex of acyclic terms compute the total derived image; generic homological algebra using the stated FullCD bound.
Steps 4 and 7: exactness of the open extension functor; a sheaf operation tool.
Step 5: Brown for an exact coproduct-preserving functor from a Grothendieck derived category; precisely the existence route, not a substituted geometric theorem.
Step 6: the section in the proper/open fibre product is clopen; an elementary geometric tool independent of cohomological comparison.
Steps 6, 8 and 9: identifies open restriction with localization of the pro-etale site and fixes its section calculation.
Step 7: computation of a total derived functor on K-injective resolutions; generic homological algebra.
Step 6: Cartesian open-extension comparison for arbitrary complexes, applied to the square with top identity and lower map b; no proper base-change theorem is used.
Steps 9 and 10: ordinary finite-level unbounded direct-image composition, including identity and associativity, for constructing coherent refinement comparisons.
Step 10: cofilteredness for already supplied compactifications over an arbitrary base, used only to remove the choice of common refinement.

Step 6 uses only its generic unbounded ringed-site direct-image localization clause, specialized to constant finite coefficients and an open site object; no smooth-purity existence-unit node states this comparison.

Steps 4 and 8: the derived open adjunction j_! -| j^* on the full ordinary pro-etale derived categories, used for coproduct preservation of j_! and full faithfulness of j_{e!}; a generic sheaf-operation tool, no existence-unit node states it.
Step 9: termwise restriction of a K-injective complex to a localized site stays K-injective; generic homological algebra on ringed sites.
